title: Claim Reversals and Re-Billing of Cash Fills under Prescription Insurance on File
content:
## When a paid claim is reversed

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**:

1. A paid claim whose fill is not picked up is reversed when the fill is returned to stock, and in any case the reversal is recorded no later than the date of service plus the class's reversal deadline days; a fill still in will-call on that day is returned to stock first.
2. A paid claim is also reversed when its fill is confirmed as a dispensing error, or to correct a billing mistake.
3. Each paid claim is reversed at most once, and the reversal books back exactly that claim's patient pay, taking it off the patient's cost share on the plan.

## Re-billing a fill paid in cash

A fill the patient paid in cash is re-billed to a coverage record added afterwards only when the fill is re-billed no later than the date the cash fill was dispensed plus the class's cash re-bill window days, counted in calendar days with the fill date as day 0. The fill date is the dispensing date on the fill record kept under Prescriptions, and the last day of the window still qualifies. The re-billed claim carries the retroactive re-bill basis, and the patient is refunded the difference between the cash paid and the new patient pay by the original payment method.

## Cash re-bill boundary (hypothetical: cash fill dispensed 5 June, 14-day window)

| Re-billed on | Day count | Within the window? |
|---|---|---|
| 18 June | day 13 | Yes |
| 19 June | day 14 | Yes — last day |
| 20 June | day 15 | No |

## Refund illustration (hypothetical amounts)

A patient paid 60.00 in cash; the re-billed claim's patient pay is 12.50. The patient is refunded 47.50 by the original payment method.

## Reversal illustration (hypothetical)

A paid claim assigned a patient pay of 15.00 and is later reversed because the fill was returned to stock. The reversal books back exactly 15.00. The same claim is not reversed a second time.
